evidence: STRUCTURE (no inversion found). task/tests/scoring.toml lines 1-11: [gates] render=0.0, constraints=0.0; [weights] functional=0.6, polish=0.2, visual=0.2; [floors] functional=0.05. scoring.toml, tools/score.py and test.sh are byte-identical to the frozen template (diff: no output; sha256 scoring.toml 95f70d6e..., score.py 13de2b38...), so the reward arithmetic is template-controlled and was not altered. score.py:41 gates_passed = all(score > 0.0); :46 weighted = sum(w*score)/sum(w); :47 floors_passed = functional > 0.05; :48 reward = weighted only if gates and floor pass, else 0. All weights positive, so reward is non-decreasing in every dimension score. Measured in my scratchpad (copy of the frozen scoring.toml + score.py, executed with python -B, nothing written to the workspace): a 7^3 grid of (functional, polish, visual) in {0, .05, .0501, .25, .5, .75, 1} with gates passing produced 0 monotonicity violations; a failed render gate with perfect scored dims gives reward 0.0 and exit 1; functional exactly 0.05 with polish=visual=1 gives 0.0 while 0.0501 gives 0.4301. Within each dimension aggregation is weighted_mean over positive criterion weights (functional 44 binary criteria, total weight 59.5; polish 5 binary, 12.0; visual 5 likert points=5 at weight 1.2 each, 6.0), so passing an extra criterion can never lower a dimension score. Function (0.6) outweighs craft (0.4 combined), which is the skill's explicit test for this row. GATES vs STRONGER APP: gates/constraints/judge.toml:23 accepts 'the Observer (prefer Aud Halvorsen; another working staff account is acceptable)', so an otherwise strong app with a broken Observer role is not zeroed by the gate; the same lenient wording is restated as the in-dimension browser gate in functional/polish/visual prompt.md line 11, so the scored gate is no stricter than the real gate. gates/render requires only wrong-password refusal plus valid Recruiter sign-in and a usable workspace (render/judge.toml:23), all public (instruction.md:17). No gate demands a hidden requirement a better app could miss. CRITERIA that could invert: rows with 'this row is 0' clauses (hro_refusal_status, hro_candidate_no_staff, hro_candidate_private, polish hro_pol_live_board/hro_pol_live_thread) zero only absent/dead features, which preserves rather than inverts ranking (REVIEW_POLICY 'a dead feature must not earn credit for doing nothing'). hro_refusal_status counts only refused replays and states that an accepted replay is deducted only in its own row, avoiding double penalty; status codes 401/403/404/409 are public (hireops_rules.md:21-23, :78). Conforming alternatives are accepted (hro_refused_put_back 'A UI that refuses before the card moves ... also passes'; hidden controls optional; polling/SSE/sockets all accepted per hireops_rules.md:117-121). Polish rows all require working live updates/messaging, so polish cannot be farmed by a non-working app; visual is gated by the same browser check (visual prompt.md:12 'minimum raw Likert score 1, which normalizes to zero'). NOTES (not defects under this row): (1) Template-controlled shaping permits a functionally thin but visually excellent app to beat a moderately functional plain app, e.g. functional 0.06 + visual 1.0 + polish 0 = 0.236 vs functional 0.35 + visual 0.0 (all Likert 1) + polish 0 = 0.21; this needs an extreme, implausible visual gap and the weights/floor are shared template policy that must not be changed to silence QC; weight honesty belongs to row 44. (2) Live-update capability is credited in both functional (hro_live_board 2.5, hro_msg_exchange 1.5, hro_unread_counts 2, hro_unread_scrolled_up 2, hro_seen 1.5 -> ~0.096 of reward) and polish (hro_pol_live_board 3 + hro_pol_live_thread 3 of 12 -> 0.10), ~0.20 total, while all authorization rows together (observer_readonly, candidate_no_staff, anonymous, refusal_status, mgr_early_refused, mgr_other_job, thread_access, candidate_private = 10.5/59.5) carry ~0.106; an insecure app with push updates can therefore outrank a secure app whose updates never arrive. Both features are public requirements (instruction.md:5, :9; hireops_rules.md section 5), the polish rows grade distinct preservation outcomes, and which app is 'worse' is a weighting judgement rather than an arithmetic inversion; flagged for the owner/row 44. (3) Evaluator-truncation inversion risk: every prompt maps an evaluator failure or exhausted budget to binary 0 / Likert 1 ('NOT EXERCISED - evaluator/tool limitation'). A complete app forces the judge through the whole long functional protocol (Z,S,M,L,C,B,N,T,U,K,R,V,A,D in 9000 s, restart LAST), whereas broken features end steps early, so budget exhaustion would preferentially zero late rows (hro_restart 1.5, hro_activity, hro_live_board) of stronger apps. This is unmeasured, not demonstrated. RUNTIME EVIDENCE: raw-evidence-index.json scope states verbatim 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent'; its entries are scripted golden browser/API observations only ('Not a configured judge run, Oracle grade, model score or judge-duration measurement'). REVIEW_POLICY requires a hash-bound reward-ordering runtime record before local clearance; none exists. I did not verify those artifact hashes further because none bears on ranking. Conclusion: no weight/gate/criterion arrangement inverts the ranking on source and arithmetic review, but actual ranking of a golden vs mutated weak apps under the configured judge is not measured, so this cannot be upgraded to Pass and risk stays true.
suggested_fix: No source change required for this row. Before clearance, record a hash-bound reward-ordering run (golden plus graded weak mutants, e.g. no-live-updates, no-authorization, plain-CSS) under the configured judge, and confirm the full functional protocol completes inside its 9000 s budget for the golden so budget truncation cannot zero a stronger app's late rows.
